reason: The nine-input, three-round screen preserves the tested outputs but does not establish a stable warm single-request latency gain on the M2 Ultra with CPU4 decoding. Paired request reductions are Q4_K 0.53%, Q8_0 0.30% and F16 0.10%, within round variation. Encoder-only reductions are retained as measured evidence; this prototype is not adopted. Full and short-prefix runs are omitted.

conditions.name: Haas on Apple Silicon
conditions.purpose: Reduce warm latency for one Japanese voice input of a few seconds to 30 seconds while preserving recognition quality.
conditions.latency_definition: Time from before sending the first PCM16 chunk through receipt of the terminal result. File reading, model loading and warmup are excluded. Each measured input is warmed once per fresh worker.
conditions.aggregation: Median over rounds for each input, then linearly interpolated p50, p90 and p99 across the measured input medians. RTFx divides total audio duration by summed request time.
conditions.literal_cer: Total Unicode code-point Levenshtein edits divided by total reference code points, including punctuation, symbols and whitespace.
conditions.repository_cer: NFKC followed by removing Unicode punctuation, symbols, separators and whitespace; no case folding or alternate-spelling substitutions. Edits and reference lengths are summed before division.
conditions.quality_comparison: The same quality files on both builds; text and public token/segment text and times are compared exactly. Text from every timestamp-disabled latency round is also compared. A changed CER is not evidence of exact output equality.
conditions.unobserved_fields: The worker does not expose raw TDT token IDs, frame indices or duration decisions. These are not claimed to match by this harness.
limitations: The current corpus is FLEURS Japanese test, with inputs from 6.36 to 28.2 seconds.
The p99 of a small duration-stratified sample is not a precise estimate of production tail latency.
The repository CER is not the published metric accepting alternative spellings of words.
Fresh-process load and first-request times do not reset filesystem or system Metal caches.
This is a nine-input screen with nine timestamped quality inputs per type. Full 30/650 and short-prefix evaluations were not run.
The three-input encoder timing improvement is separate from whole-request latency and does not establish a stable request gain.
Three transposed-activation controls are unsupported by the existing CPU reference. They pass only the original/off/on Metal differential comparison.
Backend CPU-reference checks and Metal differential checks do not replace official model stage references.
Windows Vulkan and M5 execution remain unverified; the M5-specific existing SiLU path is separate.

The frozen runner records explicit experiment overrides but does not reject every inherited GGML_* or SPEECH_* setting. No evidence of an unintended override was found, but the complete absence of such overrides was not captured at run time. Later launch validation does not retroactively prove that absence.
conditions.thread_setting_note: Four CPU threads are an explicit tuned campaign setting, not the runtime default. Unspecified threads (threads=0) use performance cores: 16 on this M2 Ultra. Code gains compare the tuned anchor and do not include the preliminary thread-tuning gain; measure 021 evaluates automatic versus four threads separately.
conditions.comparison_reference: Relative: the same e0b0bf2 speech binary with SiLU switch 1 versus 0. Cumulative: directly measured fixed anchor f976ebd.

diagnostics.title: Observed request variation across rounds
diagnostics.method: Sum the nine measured request times within each round. Range divided by the median sum describes observed round variation; it is not the median paired reduction or a confidence interval.
notes: The measured paired reductions of 0.53%, 0.30% and 0.10% are not separated from this bounded screen's variation. No full-corpus or short-prefix extension is claimed.

diagnostics.title: Separate encoder compute timings
diagnostics.method: Three timing inputs, each warmed and measured three times; the table uses the per-input median encoder compute time. These are not worker request latencies.
notes: The sub-millisecond encoder savings do not establish a stable end-to-end gain. CPU decoding uses four explicit threads throughout.
